literal: When there is no food for the ear, a little should be offered even to the stomach.
translation: When there is no food of wisdom for the ear to feast upon, only then should a little food be offered to the stomach.
modern: காதுக்குக் கேட்கும் அறிவு உணவு இல்லாத பொழுது, வயிற்றுக்கும் சிறிதளவு உணவு கொடுக்கப்பட வேண்டும்.
explanation: This couplet beautifully contrasts intellectual nourishment with physical sustenance. The poet metaphorically describes listening to wise teachings as 'food for the ear'. Physical food for the stomach is treated as a secondary necessity, to be taken only in small measures when the mind is not actively engaged in learning. By prioritizing the hunger of the ears over the hunger of the stomach, the couplet elevates the pursuit of knowledge above mere physical existence.
